SAY (~12 seconds): On Mars, dust steals power while radiation exposure adds up. NASA measured both: our challenge is helping a young learner connect these invisible quantities.

EVIDENCE: Curiosity RAD historical tissue-like detector value: 210 ± 40 microgray per Earth day, Gale Crater, August 2012–June 2013; not a human-risk limit. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20180007641 and primary manuscript https://authors.library.caltech.edu/records/kdt88-3aw98 . Pathfinder paper reports 0.28% per day decrease in short-circuit current; not a universal solar-power or per-sol coefficient. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20020031145 . Ages 7–12 are the intended audience, not a validated learning-outcome sample.

SAY (~12 seconds): Four linked relationships explain the result: cleaning changes dust, dust changes solar output, net power changes stored energy, and radiation rate accumulates into dose.

DETAIL: Multiplication assumes a constant rate over the interval; the game accumulates changing values through time. Cleaning pace and fatigue change cleaning and energy. Completed default rounds share the same outside duration and accumulated dose; the current player does not optimize final radiation dose. Gray and sievert are not interchangeable. The innovation is connecting established science through immediate feedback, not a new physical law. Rover-power research: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20230007029 ; implemented assumptions: https://github.com/roshaninfordham/NASA-SPACE-APPS-HACKATHON-2026/blob/main/docs/SCIENCE-JOURNEY-SOURCES.md
